### sender valilidation

*  email does not verify sender is genuine
   *  problem for spam
   *  would like to reject "spoofed" messages
*  some grafted-on solutions
   *  Sender Policy Framework (RFC 7208)
   *  DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) signatures (RFC 6376)
   *  Domain-Based Nessage Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (RFC 9989)

### SPF

*  `foo.com IN TXT "v=spf1 a:foo.com mx:bar.com ip:1.2.3.0/24 ~ip:1.2.0.0/16 -all`
   *  allow from `foo.com`, bar.com's MX servers, 1.2.3.0/24
   *  "softfail" from 1.2.0.0/16
   *  "fail" all others

### DomainKeys Idenitifed Mail signature {.smaller}

```
DKIM-Signature: v=1; a=rsa-sha256; q=dns/txt; d=virginia.edu; s=azout-selector; c=relaxed/relaxed;
 h=from:to:cc:subject:date:message-id:references:content-type:mime-version:reply-to:list-id:list-help:list-subscribe:list-unsubscribe:list-post:list-owner:list-archive;
 bh=vI/QgQAmn/cDF8zzsjO1mOAhmBPVjAnxw04hQqBOrH0=;
 b=...
```
*  `c=relaxes/relaxed`: normalize whitespace in headers, body before verifying signature
*  public key in DNS under `azout-selector._domainkey.virginia.edu` (s, d fields)
*  covers message headers listed in `h` field only
*  `bh=...`: hash of message body
*  `b=...` signature itself


### greylisting, blacklisting

*  greylisting (RFC 6647)
   *  give temporary errors (451) to new SMTP senders
   *  many spammers won't retry later
*  blacklisting
   *  many (usually IP-based) blacklists example: spamhaus
   *  probably means you can't run a mail server on a "home" ISP
